sanskrit: āśvāsayantaṃ bharataṃ jābālir brāhmaṇottamaḥ uvāca rāmaṃ dharmajñaṃ dharmāpetam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: While Rāma was consoling Bharata, Jābāli, the most excellent of brāhmaṇas, spoke to Rāma who was learned in dharma — these words that were devoid of dharma:

sanskrit: sādhu rāghava mā bhūt te buddhir evaṃ nirarthakā prākṛtasya narasyeva ārya buddhes tapasvinaḥ
english: "Well then, O Rāghava, let not this purposeless resolve be yours — this resolve that belongs to a common man, not to one of noble understanding and austere mind.

sanskrit: kaḥ kasya puruṣo bandhuḥ kim āpyaṃ kasya kena cit yad eko jāyate jantur eka eva vinaśyati
english: Who is any man's kinsman? What does one obtain from another? A being is born alone and perishes alone.

sanskrit: tasmān mātā pitā ceti rāma sajjeta yo naraḥ unmatta iva sa jñeyo nāsti kā cid dhi kasya cit
english: Therefore, O Rāma, the man who clings to 'mother' and 'father' should be reckoned as if deranged — there is truly no one who belongs to anyone.

sanskrit: yathā grāmāntaraṃ gacchan naraḥ kaś cit kva cid vaset utsṛjya ca tam āvāsaṃ pratiṣṭhetāpare 'hani
english: Just as a man travelling to another village lodges somewhere for a night and abandons that lodging to continue his journey the next day —

sanskrit: evam eva manuṣyāṇāṃ pitā mātā gṛhaṃ vasu āvāsamātraṃ kākutstha sajjante nātra sajjanāḥ
english: So too, O Kākutstha, a father, mother, home, and wealth are for men merely a transient lodging — the wise do not cling to them.

sanskrit: pitryaṃ rājyaṃ samutsṛjya sa nārhati narottama āsthātuṃ kāpathaṃ duḥkhaṃ viṣamaṃ bahukaṇṭakam
english: Abandoning the paternal kingdom, O foremost of men, he is not worthy to tread this painful, difficult, and thorny wrong path.

sanskrit: samṛddhāyām ayodhyāyāṃ ātmānam abhiṣecaya ekaveṇīdharā hi tvāṃ nagarī saṃpratīkṣate
english: Consecrate yourself king in the prosperous city of Ayodhyā — the city awaits you now, wearing a single braid of mourning.

sanskrit: rājabhogān anubhavan mahārhān pārthivātmaja vihara tvam ayodhyāyāṃ yathā śakras triviṣṭape
english: Enjoying the great royal pleasures befitting a king's son, sport in Ayodhyā as Śakra sports in heaven.

sanskrit: na te kaś cid daśarathaḥ tvaṃ ca tasya na kaś cana anyo rājā tvam anyaś ca tasmāt kuru yad ucyate
english: Daśaratha was nothing to you, nor were you anything to him — he was one king, you are another. Therefore do as I say.

sanskrit: gataḥ sa nṛpatis tatra gantavyaṃ yatra tena vai pravṛttir eṣā martyānāṃ tvaṃ tu mithyā vihanyase
english: That king has gone where all must go — such is the course of mortals. But you are afflicting yourself in vain.

sanskrit: arthadharmaparā ye ye tāṃs tāñ śocāmi netarān te hi duḥkham iha prāpya vināśaṃ pretya bhejire
english: Those who are devoted to artha and dharma — those I pity, not the others. For they attain suffering here and destruction in the next world.

sanskrit: aṣṭakā pitṛdaivatyam ity ayaṃ prasṛto janaḥ annasyopadravaṃ paśya mṛto hi kim aśiṣyati
english: People have spread the notion that the aṣṭakā rite is sacred to the ancestors — look at the waste of food! For what will a dead man eat?

sanskrit: yadi bhuktam ihānyena deham anyasya gacchati dadyāt pravasataḥ śrāddhaṃ na tat pathy aśanaṃ bhavet
english: If what is eaten here by one person could pass to another's body, one might give śrāddha to a traveller — but that food would not reach him on the road.

sanskrit: dānasaṃvananā hy ete granthā medhāvibhiḥ kṛtāḥ yajasva dehi dīkṣasva tapas tapyasva saṃtyaja
english: These texts saying 'sacrifice, give, consecrate yourself, perform austerities, renounce' were composed by clever men to entice people to give.

sanskrit: sa nāsti param ity eva kuru buddhiṃ mahāmate pratyakṣaṃ yat tad ātiṣṭha parokṣaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ kuru
english: Make up your mind, O great intellect, that there is no other world. Rely on what is perceptible; put the imperceptible behind you.

sanskrit: satāṃ buddhiṃ puraskṛtya sarvalokanidarśinīm rājyaṃ tvaṃ pratigṛhṇīṣva bharatena prasāditaḥ
english: Heeding the counsel of the wise, which illuminates all the world, accept the kingdom, appeased by Bharata's entreaty."

sanskrit: jābāles tu vacaḥ śrutvā rāmaḥ satyātmanāṃ varaḥ uvāca parayā yuktyā svabuddhyā cāvipannayā
english: Having heard Jābāli's words, Rāma — foremost among men of truthful nature — replied with great reason, employing his own unclouded judgement:

sanskrit: bhavān me priyakāmārthaṃ vacanaṃ yad ihoktavān akāryaṃ kāryasaṃkāśam apathyaṃ pathyasaṃmitam
english: "What you have said here with the intent of doing me good — that which is improper yet looks proper, that which is unwholesome yet seems wholesome —

sanskrit: nirmaryādas tu puruṣaḥ pāpācārasamanvitaḥ mānaṃ na labhate satsu bhinnacāritradarśanaḥ
english: A man who is without limits, given to wicked conduct, and seen to have broken character — he wins no esteem among the virtuous.

sanskrit: kulīnam akulīnaṃ vā vīraṃ puruṣamāninam cāritram eva vyākhyāti śuciṃ vā yadi vāśucim
english: Whether a man is of good lineage or bad, a hero or a braggart — it is character alone that declares him pure or impure.

sanskrit: anāryas tv āryasaṃkāśaḥ śaucād dhīnas tathā śuciḥ lakṣaṇyavad alakṣaṇyo duḥśīlaḥ śīlavān iva
english: An ignoble man may appear noble; one fallen from purity may appear pure; a man without good marks may look auspicious; a man of bad character may seem virtuous.

sanskrit: adharmaṃ dharmaveṣeṇa yadīmaṃ lokasaṃkaram abhipatsye śubhaṃ hitvā kriyāvidhivivarjitam
english: If I were to embrace this adharma dressed in the garb of dharma — this confusion of the world's order, stripped of proper rite and conducive of no good —

sanskrit: kaś cetayānaḥ puruṣaḥ kāryākāryavicakṣaṇaḥ bahu maṃsyati māṃ loke durvṛttaṃ lokadūṣaṇam
english: What discerning man, skilled in distinguishing right action from wrong, would think highly of me in the world — me, who had become wicked and a corrupter of the world?

sanskrit: kasya yāsyāmy ahaṃ vṛttaṃ kena vā svargam āpnuyām anayā vartamāno 'haṃ vṛttyā hīnapratijñayā
english: Whose conduct could I follow? How would I attain heaven, living by this mode of life and having forfeited my vow?

sanskrit: kāmavṛttas tv ayaṃ lokaḥ kṛtsnaḥ samupavartate yadvṛttāḥ santi rājānas tadvṛttāḥ santi hi prajāḥ
english: This entire world conducts itself by imitating those who act as they wish. As kings behave, so do their subjects.

sanskrit: satyam evānṛśaṃsyaṃ ca rājavṛttaṃ sanātanam tasmāt satyātmakaṃ rājyaṃ satye lokaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ
english: Truth and freedom from cruelty — this is the eternal conduct of kings. Therefore kingship is grounded in truth, and the world is established in truth.

sanskrit: ṛṣayaś caiva devāś ca satyam eva hi menire satyavādī hi loke 'smin paramaṃ gacchati kṣayam
english: The sages and the gods have held truth alone to be supreme. In this world, one who speaks truth attains the highest abode.

sanskrit: udvijante yathā sarpān narād anṛtavādinaḥ dharmaḥ satyaṃ paro loke mūlaṃ svargasya cocyate
english: Men recoil from a liar just as from a serpent. Truth is the supreme dharma in the world; it is said to be the very root of heaven.

sanskrit: satyam eveśvaro loke satyaṃ padmā samāśritā satyamūlāni sarvāṇi satyān nāsti paraṃ padam
english: Truth alone is the sovereign of the world; upon truth does Lakṣmī herself rest. All things are rooted in truth; there is no station higher than truth.

sanskrit: dattam iṣṭaṃ hutaṃ caiva taptāni ca tapāṃsi ca vedāḥ satyapratiṣṭhānās tasmāt satyaparo bhavet
english: Gifts given, sacrifices performed, oblations offered, austerities endured, and the Vedas — all are established in truth. Therefore one should be devoted to truth.

sanskrit: ekaḥ pālayate lokam ekaḥ pālayate kulam majjaty eko hi niraya ekaḥ svarge mahīyate
english: One man sustains an entire world; one man upholds a family. One man sinks into hell; one man is exalted in heaven.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ pitur nideśaṃ tu kimarthaṃ nānupālaye satyapratiśravaḥ satyaṃ satyena samayīkṛtaḥ
english: Why then should I not honour my father's command? — I, who am pledged to truth, who ratified that pledge by truth itself with truth.

sanskrit: naiva lobhān na mohād vā na cājñānāt tamo'nvitaḥ setuṃ satyasya bhetsyāmi guroḥ satyapratiśravaḥ
english: Neither from greed, nor from delusion, nor from ignorance shrouded in darkness will I break the embankment of truth — I who have pledged truth to my father.

sanskrit: asatyasaṃdhasya sataś calasyāsthiracetasaḥ naiva devā na pitaraḥ pratīcchantīti naḥ śrutam
english: We have heard it said that neither gods nor ancestors accept the offerings of one who has bound himself to falsehood, who is fickle, and whose mind is unsteady.

sanskrit: pratyagātmam imaṃ dharmaṃ satyaṃ paśyāmy ahaṃ svayam bhāraḥ satpuruṣācīrṇas tad artham abhinandyate
english: This dharma — truth — I myself perceive as turning toward the inner self. That burden trodden by virtuous men is to be embraced for its own sake.

sanskrit: kṣātraṃ dharmam ahaṃ tyakṣye hy adharmaṃ dharmasaṃhitam kṣudraur nṛśaṃsair lubdhaiś ca sevitaṃ pāpakarmabhiḥ
english: I will not abandon the kṣatriya dharma to take up adharma that merely resembles dharma — that which is practised by the base, the cruel, the greedy, and the wicked.

sanskrit: kāyena kurute pāpaṃ manasā saṃpradhārya ca anṛtaṃ jihvayā cāha trividhaṃ karma pātakam
english: One commits sin with the body, having deliberated with the mind, and speaks untruth with the tongue — these three are the sinful deeds of the three faculties.

sanskrit: bhūmiḥ kīrtir yaśo lakṣmīḥ puruṣaṃ prārthayanti hi svargasthaṃ cānubadhnanti satyam eva bhajeta tat
english: The earth, fame, glory, and Lakṣmī seek out a man of truth; even those dwelling in heaven follow him. Therefore one should adhere to truth alone.

sanskrit: śreṣṭhaṃ hy anāryam eva syād yad bhavān avadhārya mām āha yuktikarair vākyair idaṃ bhadraṃ kuruṣva ha
english: For what you said to me, urging me with seemingly reasoned words — 'do this good thing' — would have been the most ignoble course.

sanskrit: kathaṃ hy ahaṃ pratijñāya vanavāsam imaṃ guroḥ bharatasya kariṣyāmi vaco hitvā guror vacaḥ
english: How could I, having vowed this forest-dwelling to my father, do Bharata's bidding by abandoning my father's word?

sanskrit: sthirā mayā pratijñātā pratijñā gurusaṃnidhau prahṛṣṭamānasā devī kaikeyī cābhavat tadā
english: That vow was firmly made by me in my father's presence, and at that moment Queen Kaikeyī was filled with joy.

sanskrit: vanavāsaṃ vasann evaṃ śucir niyatabhojanaḥ mūlaiḥ puṣpaiḥ phalaiḥ puṇyaiḥ pitṝn devāṃś ca tarpayan
english: Living thus in the forest, pure, eating with restraint, satisfying the ancestors and gods with holy roots, flowers, and fruits —

sanskrit: saṃtuṣṭapañcavargo 'haṃ lokayātrāṃ pravartaye akuhaḥ śraddadhānaḥ san kāryākāryavicakṣaṇaḥ
english: — I, with the five senses fully content, set forth on life's journey without deceit, full of faith, discerning what ought and ought not to be done.

sanskrit: karmabhūmim imāṃ prāpya kartavyaṃ karma yac chubham agnir vāyuś ca somaś ca karmaṇāṃ phalabhāginaḥ
english: Having attained this field of action, one must perform whatever auspicious action is to be done. Fire, wind, and the moon share in the fruits of one's deeds.

sanskrit: śataṃ kratūnām āhṛtya devarāṭ tridivaṃ gataḥ tapāṃsy ugrāṇi cāsthāya divaṃ yātā maharṣayaḥ
english: The king of the gods ascended to heaven by performing a hundred sacrifices; and the great seers attained heaven by undertaking fierce austerities.

sanskrit: satyaṃ ca dharmaṃ ca parākramaṃ ca bhūtānukampāṃ priyavāditāṃ ca dvijātidevātithipūjanaṃ ca panthānam āhus tridivasya santaḥ
english: Truth, dharma, valour, compassion for all beings, gentle speech, and the honouring of brāhmaṇas, gods, and guests — the virtuous declare these to be the path to the three heavens.

sanskrit: dharme ratāḥ satpuruṣaiḥ sametās tejasvino dānaguṇapradhānāḥ ahiṃsakā vītamalāś ca loke bhavanti pūjyā munayaḥ pradhānāḥ
english: Those sages who delight in dharma, who associate with the virtuous, who are full of lustre, foremost in the virtue of giving, non-violent, and free from stain — they are worshipped as the foremost in the world.

sanskrit: kruddham ājñāya rāmaṃ tu vasiṣṭhaḥ pratyuvāca ha jābālir api jānīte lokasyāsya gatāgatim nivartayitukāmas tu tvām etad vākyam abravīt
english: Perceiving that Rāma was angered, Vasiṣṭha replied: "Jābāli too understands the comings and goings of this world — he spoke these words only wishing to turn you back."

sanskrit: imāṃ lokasamutpattiṃ lokanātha nibodha me sarvaṃ salilam evāsīt pṛthivī yatra nirmitā tataḥ samabhavad brahmā svayambhūr daivataiḥ saha
english: "Hear from me, O lord of the world, the origin of this world. All was water in the beginning; from it the earth was fashioned. Then Brahmā, the self-born, arose together with the gods.

sanskrit: sa varāhas tato bhūtvā projjahāra vasuṃdharām asṛjac ca jagat sarvaṃ saha putraiḥ kṛtātmabhiḥ
english: He then became a boar and lifted up the earth; and with his sons of purified souls he created the entire world.

sanskrit: ākāśaprabhavo brahmā śāśvato nitya avyayaḥ tasmān marīciḥ saṃjajñe marīceḥ kaśyapaḥ sutaḥ
english: Brahmā, born of space, is eternal, constant, and imperishable. From him was born Marīci; from Marīci, Kaśyapa was born as a son.

sanskrit: vivasvān kaśyapāj jajñe manur vaivasvataḥ smṛtaḥ sa tu prajāpatiḥ pūrvam ikṣvākus tu manoḥ sutaḥ
english: From Kaśyapa was born Vivasvān; from Vivasvān came Manu, known as Vaivasvata. He was the first Prajāpati; from Manu came Ikṣvāku as a son.

sanskrit: yasyeyaṃ prathamaṃ dattā samṛddhā manunā mahī tam ikṣvākum ayodhyāyāṃ rājānaṃ viddhi pūrvakam
english: Know that Ikṣvāku, to whom this prosperous earth was first given by Manu, was the primordial king in Ayodhyā.

sanskrit: ikṣvākos tu sutaḥ śrīmān kukṣir eveti viśrutaḥ kukṣer athātmajo vīro vikukṣir udapadyata
english: The glorious son of Ikṣvāku was known as Kukṣi; from Kukṣi was born the heroic son Vikukṣi.

sanskrit: vikukṣes tu mahātejā bāṇaḥ putraḥ pratāpavān bāṇasya tu mahābāhur anaraṇyo mahāyaśāḥ
english: From Vikukṣi came the greatly lustrous and valiant son Bāṇa; from Bāṇa came the long-armed Anaraṇya of great renown.

sanskrit: nānāvṛṣṭir babhūvāsmin na durbhikṣaṃ satāṃ vare anaraṇye mahārāje taskaro vāpi kaś cana
english: During the reign of the great king Anaraṇya, O best of the virtuous, there was neither erratic rainfall nor famine, nor any thief whatsoever.

sanskrit: anaraṇyān mahābāhuḥ pṛthū rājā babhūva ha tasmāt pṛthor mahārājas triśaṅkur udapadyata sa satyavacanād vīraḥ saśarīro divaṃ gataḥ
english: From Anaraṇya came King Pṛthu of mighty arms; from that great king Pṛthu came Triśaṅku — who, heroic by virtue of his truthful word, ascended to heaven in his own body.

sanskrit: triśaṅkor abhavat sūnur dhundhumāro mahāyaśāḥ dhundhumārān mahātejā yuvanāśvo vyajāyata
english: Triśaṅku's son was the greatly renowned Dhundhumāra; from Dhundhumāra was born the greatly lustrous Yuvanāśva.

sanskrit: yuvanāśva sutaḥ śrīmān māndhātā samapadyata māndhātus tu mahātejāḥ susaṃdhir udapadyata
english: From Yuvanāśva was born the glorious son Māndhātā; from the greatly lustrous Māndhātā came Susaṃdhi.

sanskrit: susaṃdher api putrau dvau dhruvasaṃdhiḥ prasenajit yaśasvī dhruvasaṃdhes tu bharato ripusūdanaḥ
english: Susaṃdhi had two sons: Dhruvasaṃdhi and Prasenajit. From the glorious Dhruvasaṃdhi came Bharata, destroyer of enemies.

sanskrit: bharatāt tu mahābāhor asito nāma jāyata yasyaite pratirājāna udapadyanta śatravaḥ haihayās tālajaṅghāś ca śūrāś ca śaśabindavaḥ
english: From the long-armed Bharata was born one named Asita, against whom arose these rival kings as enemies: the Haihayas, the Tālajaṅghas, the Śūras, and the Śaśabindus.

sanskrit: tāṃs tu sarvān prativyūhya yuddhe rājā pravāsitaḥ sa ca śailavare ramye babhūvābhirato muniḥ dve cāsya bhārye garbhiṇyau babhūvatur iti śrutiḥ
english: Having arrayed against all of them in battle, the king was driven into exile; he dwelt as an ascetic, content on a beautiful mountain. Both his wives were pregnant, so tradition relates.

sanskrit: bhārgavaś cyavano nāma himavantam upāśritaḥ tam ṛṣiṃ samupāgamya kālindī tv abhyavādayat
english: A Bhārgava named Cyavana dwelt on the Himālayas. Kālindī approached that sage and saluted him.

sanskrit: sa tām abhyavadad vipro varepsuṃ putrajanmani tataḥ sā gṛham āgamya devī putraṃ vyajāyata
english: The brahmin blessed her, she who was hoping for the boon of a son's birth. Then that queen returned home and gave birth to a son.

sanskrit: sapatnyā tu garas tasyai datto garbhajighāṃsayā gareṇa saha tenaiva jātaḥ sa sagaro 'bhavat
english: But by her co-wife, poison had been given to her, intending to destroy the foetus. Born together with that poison, he became known as Sagara.

sanskrit: sa rājā sagaro nāma yaḥ samudram akhānayat iṣṭvā parvaṇi vegena trāsayantam imāḥ prajāḥ
english: That king, named Sagara, had the ocean dug; he performed sacrifice with intensity, terrifying these subjects.

sanskrit: asamañjas tu putro 'bhūt sagarasyeti naḥ śrutam jīvann eva sa pitrā tu nirastaḥ pāpakarmakṛt
english: Sagara's son, so we have heard, was Asamañjas — a doer of wicked deeds, banished by his father while still living.

sanskrit: aṃśumān iti putro 'bhūd asamañjasya vīryavān dilīpo 'ṃśumataḥ putro dilīpasya bhagīrathaḥ
english: The valiant son of Asamañjas was Aṃśumān; the son of Aṃśumān was Dilīpa; from Dilīpa came Bhagīratha.

sanskrit: bhagīrathāt kakutsthas tu kākutsthā yena tu smṛtāḥ kakutsthasya tu putro 'bhūd raghur yena tu rāghavaḥ
english: From Bhagīratha came Kakutstha, from whom the Kākutsthas are remembered; the son of Kakutstha was Raghu, from whom the Rāghavas take their name.

sanskrit: raghos tu putras tejasvī pravṛddhaḥ puruṣādakaḥ kalmāṣapādaḥ saudāsa ity evaṃ prathito bhuvi
english: The lustrous son of Raghu, grown great and given to devouring men, was known on earth as Kalmāṣapāda or Saudāsa.

sanskrit: kalmāṣapādaputro 'bhūc chaṅkhaṇas tv iti viśrutaḥ yas tu tad vīryam āsādya sahaseno vyanīnaśat
english: Kalmāṣapāda's son was known as Śaṅkhaṇa; possessing that valour, Sahasena came to ruin.

sanskrit: śaṅkhaṇasya tu putro 'bhūc chūraḥ śrīmān sudarśanaḥ sudarśanasyāgnivarṇa agnivarṣasya śīghragaḥ
english: The son of Śaṅkhaṇa was the heroic and glorious Sudarśana; from Sudarśana came Agnivarṇa; from Agnivarṣa came Śīghraga.

sanskrit: śīghragasya maruḥ putro maroḥ putraḥ praśuśrukaḥ praśuśrukasya putro 'bhūd ambarīṣo mahādyutiḥ
english: The son of Śīghraga was Maru; the son of Maru was Praśuśruka; the son of Praśuśruka was the greatly radiant Ambarīṣa.

sanskrit: ambarīṣasya putro 'bhūn nahuṣaḥ satyavikramaḥ nahuṣasya ca nābhāgaḥ putraḥ paramadhārmikaḥ
english: Ambarīṣa's son was Nahuṣa, of true valour; and the son of Nahuṣa was Nābhāga, supremely righteous.

sanskrit: ajaś ca suvrataś caiva nābhāgasya sutāv ubhau ajasya caiva dharmātmā rājā daśarathaḥ sutaḥ
english: Nābhāga had two sons: Aja and Suvrata; and the righteous king Daśaratha was the son of Aja.

sanskrit: tasya jyeṣṭho 'si dāyādo rāma ity abhiviśrutaḥ tad gṛhāṇa svakaṃ rājyam avekṣasva jagan nṛpa
english: You are his eldest heir, O Rāma, widely proclaimed as such. Therefore receive your own kingdom and look after the world, O king.

sanskrit: ikṣvākūṇāṃ hi sarveṣāṃ rājā bhavati pūrvajaḥ pūrvaje nāvaraḥ putro jyeṣṭho rājye 'bhiṣicyate
english: For among all the Ikṣvākus the firstborn becomes king; when the elder is living, no younger son is consecrated in the kingdom — the eldest is installed.

sanskrit: sa rāghavāṇāṃ kuladharmam ātmanaḥ sanātanaṃ nādya vihātum arhasi prabhūtaratnām anuśādhi medinīṃ prabhūtarāṣṭrāṃ pitṛvan mahāyaśāḥ
english: Therefore, O man of great glory, you should not today abandon the eternal family dharma of the Rāghavas and of yourself — rule this earth, rich in jewels and rich in kingdoms, as your father did."
